survey: A stone chess table on grass, seen from slightly above and turned about 45° so that two corners point toward the viewer. The square top slab has a thick rim. Its two visible side faces run along two directions, about 19° and 157° on the page. A recessed checkerboard is set into the top, and its rows of tiles run along those same two directions. The tiles stay close to the same size, which suits this near-isometric, mildly stylized view. A square pedestal sits under the centre of the top. Its corners are vertical, and its top and bottom edges follow the same two directions as the slab. The pedestal stands on a thin square base plate that lies flat on the grass and is turned the same way. Two round stone stools stand beside the table, one partly hidden behind its back-left corner and one at front right. Each stool has a cap with an elliptical top over a slightly flaring trunk, with vertical sides. The front-right stool's top ellipse is roughly 0.4 as tall as it is wide. That fits the downward view implied by the table top's foreshortening. All parts sit on the same ground plane, and the base plate and both stools meet the grass at the angle the ground is drawn.
